parsing_res_list.block_content: ## SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL: ROBUST BACKUP CONTROLLER AND BACKUP SET FOR THE UNCERTAIN PLANAR QUADROTOR MODEL
To simplify the notation used in this section, we use  $ \lambda_{\min}(S) $ and  $ \lambda_{\max}(S) $ to denote the smallest and largest eigenvalues of a symmetric matrix S, and we define

$$ \begin{aligned}&a_{m}(\boldsymbol{\theta})\triangleq\frac{1}{m_{0}}+\delta_{m},\quad a_{J}(\boldsymbol{\theta})\triangleq\frac{1}{J_{0}}+\delta_{J},\quad\boldsymbol{e}_{1}\triangleq\left[\begin{array}{cc}{{{0}}}&{{{1}}} \\{{{1}}}&{{{0}}}\end{array}\right]^{\top},\\&\boldsymbol{K}_{\vartheta}\triangleq\left[\boldsymbol{k}_{\vartheta}\quad\boldsymbol{k}_{\omega}\right],\quad\boldsymbol{b}_{\vartheta}\triangleq\left[\begin{array}{cc}{{{0}}}&{{{1}}}\end{array}\right]^{\top},\quad\boldsymbol{A}_{\vartheta}(a)\triangleq\begin{bmatrix}{{{0}}}&{{{1}}} \\{{{-a k_{\vartheta}}}}&{{{-a k_{\omega}}}}\end{bmatrix},\\&\Delta_{\vartheta}\triangleq\sqrt{\varrho_{\vartheta}\boldsymbol{e}_{1}^{\top}\boldsymbol{P}_{\vartheta}^{-1}\boldsymbol{e}_{1}},\quad\Delta_{M}\triangleq\sqrt{\varrho_{\vartheta}\boldsymbol{K}_{\vartheta}\boldsymbol{P}_{\vartheta}^{-1}\boldsymbol{K}_{\vartheta}^{\top}},\quad\bar{\vartheta}\triangleq\vartheta_{\mathrm{r}}+\Delta_{\vartheta}.\\&Then,parameter bounds in Assumption 1 induce known\\&constants satisfying\\ \end{aligned} $$

$$ \begin{align*}&\delta_{g}^{-}\leq\delta_{g}\leq\delta_{g}^{+},\quad\delta_{\ell}^{-}\leq\delta_{\ell}\leq\delta_{\ell}^{+},\\&0<a_{J}^{-}\leq a_{J}(\boldsymbol{\varTheta})\leq a_{J}^{+},\quad0<a_{m}^{-}\leq a_{m}(\boldsymbol{\varTheta})\leq a_{m}^{+},\end{align*} $$

for all  $ \theta \in \Theta $. The proposition below provides sufficient conditions on the design parameters of the backup controller (38) and the backup set (39) for Assumption 2 to hold for the uncertain quadrotor model (36).

Proposition 1. Consider the uncertain quadrotor model (36), the safety function (37) with the safe set  $ C_S $, the backup controller (38), and the backup set  $ C_B $ in (39). If the controller gains  $ k_\vartheta > 0 $,  $ k_\omega > 0 $ and the design parameters  $ P_\vartheta = P_\vartheta^\top \succ 0 $,  $ Q_\vartheta = Q_\vartheta^\top \succ 0 $,  $ \varrho_\vartheta > 0 $,  $ \vartheta_\tau \in (0, \vartheta_{\max}) $,  $ r_x $,  $ r_z > 0 $, and  $ r_\vartheta \in (0, \vartheta_{\max}^2) $, with  $ \bar{\vartheta} < \pi/2 $, are chosen such that

$$ \begin{aligned}&\mathcal{A}_{\vartheta}(a_{J}^{-})^{\top}\mathcal{P}_{\vartheta}+\mathcal{P}_{\vartheta}\mathcal{A}_{\vartheta}(a_{J}^{-})\preceq-\mathcal{Q}_{\vartheta},\\&\mathcal{A}_{\vartheta}(a_{J}^{+})^{\top}\mathcal{P}_{\vartheta}+\mathcal{P}_{\vartheta}\mathcal{A}_{\vartheta}(a_{J}^{+})\preceq-\mathcal{Q}_{\vartheta},\\&\Delta_{M}\leq M_{\max},\\&\vartheta_{\mathrm{r}}-\Delta_{\vartheta}\geq0,\\&\vartheta_{\mathrm{r}}+\Delta_{\vartheta}\leq\sqrt{\vartheta_{\max}^{2}-r_{\vartheta}},\\&\varrho_{\vartheta}\geq\lambda_{\max}(\mathcal{P}_{\vartheta})\left(\frac{2\left\|\mathcal{P}_{\vartheta}\boldsymbol{b}_{\vartheta}\right\|F_{\max}\max\{\left|\delta_{\ell}^{-}\right|,\left|\delta_{\ell}^{+}\right|\}_{\mathrm{J}}}{\lambda_{\min}(\mathcal{Q}_{\vartheta})}\right)^{2}\\&a_{m}^{-}F_{\max}\cos(\bar{\vartheta})-g_{0}-\delta_{g}^{+}\geq0,\\&\mathrm{e}^{-\kappa r_{x}}+\mathrm{e}^{-\kappa r_{z}}+\mathrm{e}^{-\kappa r_{\vartheta}}\leq1,\end{aligned} $$

then the moment saturation in (38) is inactive on  $ \mathcal{C}_B $,  $ \mathcal{C}_B \subseteq \mathcal{C}_S $ holds, and the backup controller (38) renders  $ \mathcal{C}_B $ robustly forward invariant for (36) for all  $ \theta \in \Theta $, i.e., Assumption 2 is satisfied.

Proof. We first consider the pitch dynamics. On the set  $ \mathcal{C}_\mathrm{B} $,  $ h_{\vartheta,\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x}) \geq 0 $ implies  $ \boldsymbol{y}_\vartheta^\top \boldsymbol{P}_\vartheta \boldsymbol{y}_\vartheta \leq \varrho_\vartheta $, and hence
$$ |\vartheta-\vartheta_{\mathrm{r}}|\leq\Delta_{\vartheta},\quad|\boldsymbol{K}_{\vartheta}\boldsymbol{y}_{\vartheta}|\leq\Delta_{M}. $$

Thus, by the fourth and fifth conditions in (40), the pitch angle satisfies  $ 0 \leq \vartheta \leq \bar{\vartheta} \leq \sqrt{\vartheta_{\max}^2 - r_\vartheta} $ on  $ C_B $. Moreover, the third condition in (40) yields  $ |K_\vartheta y_\vartheta| \leq M_{\max} $, and hence the moment saturation in (38) is inactive on  $ C_B $.
We next verify the robust invariance of the pitch dynamics under the backup controller, which satisfy
$$ \begin{array}{r}{\dot{\mathbf{y}}_{\vartheta}=A_{\vartheta}(a_{J}(\boldsymbol{\theta}))\mathbf{y}_{\vartheta}+\mathbf{b}_{\vartheta}\delta_{\ell}F_{\operatorname*{m a x}}.}\end{array} $$
Since  $ A_{\vartheta}(a) $ depends affinely on a, the first two conditions in (40) imply
$$ \boldsymbol{A}_{\vartheta}(a)^{\top}\boldsymbol{P}_{\vartheta}+\boldsymbol{P}_{\vartheta}\boldsymbol{A}_{\vartheta}(a)\preceq-\boldsymbol{Q}_{\vartheta},\forall a\in[a_{J}^{-},a_{J}^{+}]. $$
Therefore, with  $ V_\vartheta \triangleq y_\vartheta^\top P_\vartheta y_\vartheta $, we have

$$ \begin{aligned}\dot{V}_{\vartheta}&=\boldsymbol{y}_{\vartheta}^{\top}\big(\boldsymbol{A}_{\vartheta}(a_{J}(\boldsymbol{\theta}))^{\top}\boldsymbol{P}_{\vartheta}+\boldsymbol{P}_{\vartheta}\boldsymbol{A}_{\vartheta}(a_{J}(\boldsymbol{\theta}))\big)\boldsymbol{y}_{\vartheta}\\&+2\boldsymbol{y}_{\vartheta}^{\top}\boldsymbol{P}_{\vartheta}\boldsymbol{b}_{\vartheta}\delta_{\ell}\boldsymbol{F}_{\max}\end{aligned} $$

$$ \leq-\lambda_{\min}(Q_{\vartheta})\|\boldsymbol{y}_{\vartheta}\|^{2}+2F_{\max}\|\boldsymbol{P}_{\vartheta}\boldsymbol{b}_{\vartheta}\|\max\{|\delta_{\ell}^{-}|,|\delta_{\ell}^{+}|\}\|\boldsymbol{y}_{\vartheta}\|. $$

On the boundary  $ h_{\vartheta,\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x})=0 $, we have  $ V_{\vartheta}=\varrho_{\vartheta} $, and hence  $ \|\boldsymbol{y}_{\vartheta}\|\geq\sqrt{\varrho_{\vartheta}/\lambda_{\max}(\boldsymbol{P}_{\vartheta})}>0 $. Therefore, by the sixth condition in (40),  $ \dot{V}_{\vartheta}\leq0 $ on the boundary of the zero superlevel set of  $ h_{\vartheta,\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x}) $. Equivalently,  $ \dot{h}_{\vartheta,\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x})\geq0 $ on this boundary, and the pitch component of  $ C_{\mathrm{B}} $ is robustly forward invariant.
We now consider the horizontal component of the motion. Since  $ 0 \leq \vartheta \leq \bar{\vartheta} < \pi/2 $ on  $ C_B $, the horizontal dynamics of (36) under (38) satisfy
$$ \dot{v}_{x}=a_{m}(\boldsymbol{\theta})F_{\max}\sin(\vartheta)-c_{x}v_{x}. $$
On the boundary  $ h_{v_{x},b}(x)=0 $, we have  $ v_{x}=0 $, and therefore
$$ \dot{h}_{v_{x},\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x})=a_{m}(\boldsymbol{\theta})F_{\mathrm{m a x}}\sin(\vartheta)\geq0, $$

where we used  $ a_m(\boldsymbol{\theta}) > 0 $ and  $ \vartheta \geq 0 $. Hence, the  $ v_x $ component of  $ \mathcal{C}_B $ is robustly forward invariant. Moreover, on  $ \mathcal{C}_B $,  $ v_x \geq 0 $, and hence  $ \dot{h}_{x,b}(\boldsymbol{x}) = v_x \geq 0 $. Therefore, the surface clearance component of  $ \mathcal{C}_B $ is robustly forward invariant.
We next consider the altitude component of the motion. On the boundary  $ h_{v_{z},b}(\boldsymbol{x})=0 $, we have  $ v_{z}=0 $, and the vertical dynamics of (36) satisfy

$$ \begin{align*}\dot{h}_{v_{z},\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x})&=\dot{v}_{z}=-g_{0}-\delta_{g}+a_{m}(\boldsymbol{\theta})F_{\mathrm{max}}\cos(\vartheta)\\&\geq-g_{0}-\delta_{g}^{+}+a_{m}^{-}F_{\mathrm{max}}\cos(\bar{\vartheta})\geq0,\end{align*} $$

where we used  $ 0 \leq \vartheta \leq \bar{\vartheta} < \pi/2 $ and the seventh condition in (40). Therefore, the  $ v_z $ component of  $ C_B $ is robustly forward invariant. Furthermore, on  $ C_B $,  $ v_z \geq 0 $, thus  $ \dot{h}_{z,\mathrm{b}}(\boldsymbol{x}) = v_z \geq 0 $, and the altitude clearance component of  $ C_B $ is also robustly forward invariant.

Finally, we show that  $ \mathcal{C}_B \subseteq \mathcal{C}_S $. Since  $ h_{x,b}(\boldsymbol{x}) \geq 0 $ and  $ h_{z,b}(\boldsymbol{x}) \geq 0 $, we have  $ h_x(\boldsymbol{x}) \geq r_x $ and  $ h_z(\boldsymbol{x}) \geq r_z $. Moreover, by the fifth condition in (40),  $ h_{\vartheta,b}(\boldsymbol{x}) \geq 0 $ implies  $ h_{\vartheta}(\boldsymbol{x}) = \vartheta_{\max}^2 - \vartheta^2 \geq r_\vartheta $. Therefore, by the last condition in (40), the smooth minimum safety function (37) satisfies  $ h(\boldsymbol{x}) \geq 0 $ for all  $ \boldsymbol{x} \in \mathcal{C}_B $, i.e.,  $ \mathcal{C}_B \subseteq \mathcal{C}_S $.

Combining the pitch, horizontal, and altitude invariance results with the input admissibility and  $ C_B \subseteq C_S $, the backup controller (38) renders the backup set (39) robustly forward invariant for (36) for all  $ \theta \in \Theta $.
